source: M5 P4, the classic's desk sitting, 2026-09-11 05:06-05:12 (local), first of the sitting's four payloads. note:
THE ROM AND THE SECOND-STAGE BOOTLOADER HALF of one image's two transcripts. `board::esp32v3::init` reprograms clkdiv mid-stream, so the ROM and the ESP-IDF bootloader talk at 115200 and the application at 921600; this capture is the first rate and `silicon-esp32v3-2026-09-11-c976f17a9-921600.txt` is the second. Neither can read the other's bytes.

EVERY CAPTURE IS A SECOND BOOT. espflash hard-resets after writing, so the boot that formatted `lpfs` in the freshly written image had already happened before this reader opened the port; the emulated twin needs a two-run recipe (`second_boot` on the classic's `boot-idle` arm) to reach the same state, or it reports the first boot's `largest_free=106494`, 2032 B short, for a reason that has nothing to do with the model.

THE COMMITTED .txt IS BYTES [0, 2268) of the 2531-byte raw read at `raw/silicon-esp32v3-2026-09-11-c976f17a9-115200.raw.bin`, which is preserved whole and untouched. The 263 trimmed bytes are the tail: the application reprogramming clkdiv to 921600 and printing its `[INIT]` chain into a reader still shifting at 115200, which is not decodable text. Every byte kept is unchanged from the wire, in the same order.

WHAT IS IN IT, AND WHAT A ROM-UP TWIN MUST REPRODUCE: the mask ROM banner `ets Jul 29 2019 12:21:46`, `rst:0x1 (POWERON_RESET),boot:0x13 (SPI_FAST_FLASH_BOOT)`, `configsip: 0, SPIWP:0xee`, `mode:DIO, clock div:2`, the three `load:`/`entry` lines, the ESP-IDF `v5.1-beta1-378-gea5e0ff298-dirt 2nd stage bootloader` (espflash's bundled one) with `chip revision: v3.1`, the partition table, SEVEN `esp_image: segment` lines (0-6), `Loaded app from partition at offset 0x10000`, and the benign `E boot: Image contains multiple DROM segments. Only the last one will be mapped.` — printed on every boot of this image, and a ROM-up twin that does not print it is not this image's twin.

THREE SAMPLES WERE TAKEN AT THIS BAUD (a, b, c; this file is a). The decodable span was 2268 bytes in all three and the three bodies are IDENTICAL byte for byte from `ets Jul 29 2019` onward. The only difference is what sat in the bridge's buffer at the instant of reset: samples b and c open on a fragment of the previous run's 921600 traffic (`[INFO] fw_esp32_common::server_` misread at 115200) where sample a opens on a fragment of the ROM banner itself. Nothing in the bootloader's own output drifts — every `I (NN)` timestamp, every segment length, every address is the same in all three.

HAND-FILED, NOT RUNNER-WRITTEN, AND THE REASON IS A FINDING. `lp-cli validate record v3-boot --config silicon:esp32v3` was run first (its --dry-run plan is in the PR body) and REFUSED to record: the classic's `boot-idle` sentinel `[stack] heartbeat: high-water` is ELICITED — `esp32_memory_stats` prints the triple only when a host asks — and the silicon driver has no sender. `host_script` (`lp-emu/lp-emu-validate/walks/v3-stop-all.script`) is passed to `--uart0-script` on the emulated plan only, so on silicon the stimulus never goes out and the sentinel never arrives. The runner's plan also SIGINTed espflash mid-write at its default `--timeout-secs 120`: the classic's 4 MB write alone takes 2 min 27 s over this cable, and the sentinel clock covers the flash. Both are M5 P6/P7 items; this sidecar is d-desk-batch.md's §6 fallback and says so rather than passing itself off as the runner's.
